void.string: Acoustic backscatter in the water column

Includes all parameters covering the strength of acoustic signal return, including absolute measurements of returning signal strength as well as parameters expressed as backscatter (the proportion of transmitted signal returned)
Acoustic noise in the water column
Parameters quantifying the magnitude of earth movements resulting from artificial sources (such as explosions) far away from the measurement site.

Measurements of air pressure as the dependent variable (ie excluding air pressure measured to specify the z co-ordinate of a balloon or sonde), including derived parameters such as tendency (rate of change) and related parameters such as air density.
Parameters quantifying the degree of hotness of the atmosphere. Specifically excludes indirect measurements of other parameters such as wet bulb temperatures.
Alkalinity, acidity and pH of the water column
Parameters quantifying the hydrogen ion concentration in water bodies
Parameters quantifying the amount of organic compounds containing both a carboxyl group and an amino group in unlithified seabed material.
Ammonium concentration parameters in the water column
Ammonium concentration parameters (including statistical parameters such as standard deviation) in the water column
Fluxes of chemical species from the atmosphere to sea or land surface including precipitation and aerosol deposition but excluding fluxes due to exchange of gases
Parameters quantifying and describing the release of substances into the atmosphere as a result of human activity
Parameters that either quantify the water content of moist air or are specifically used in its determination (eg wet bulb air temperature)
Parameters quantifying and categorising the particulate phases (solids and aerosols) of the atmosphere, excluding chemical composition
Parameters relating to atmospheric clarity, such as optical transmittance/attenuance, and resultant visibility
Any enumeration of bacteria (Kingdom Monera so includes cyanobacteria) designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. total) in any soil or sediment.
Bacteria generic abundance in water bodies
Any enumeration of bacteria (Kingdom Monera so includes cyanobacteria) designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. total) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Parameters relating to the abundance and nature of bacteria (Kingdom Monera) infecting other biota.

Parameters describing the size, shape or physiological activity of bacteria, defined as Kingdom Monera (includes cyanobacteria). Includes parameters both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.
Bacteria non taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column

Basically any bacteria carbon biomass parameters that aren't included in parameter group BATC because they cannot be mapped to specific taxa in the ITIS taxonomy. Bacteria are defined as Kingdom Monera, which includes cyanobacteria.
Bacteria non taxonomy-related biomass expressed as protein per unit volume of the water column
Any enumeration of bacteria (Kingdom Monera so includes cyanobacteria) designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus, family) in any soil or sediment.
Bacteria taxonomic abundance in water bodies
Any enumeration of bacteria (Kingdom Monera so includes cyanobacteria) designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus, family) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Bacteria taxonomy-related ash-free dry weight biomass in sediment

Bacteria ash-free dry weight biomass in sediment parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. The taxa may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards. Bacteria are defined as all taxa that fall into Kingdom Monera in the ITIS taxonomy, which includes cyanobacteria.
Bacteria taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column

Bacteria carbon biomass parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards. Bacteria are defined as all taxa that fall into Kingdom Monera in the ITIS taxonomy, which includes cyanobacteria.
Bacterial consumption in the water column
Bacterial production in the water column
Parameters related to bacterial production determination by measurement of dissolved organic molecule (e.g. leucine, thymidine) uptake rates
Depth of the water column or elevation of land surface relative to sea surface, geoid or other datum
Parameters describing the effects of substances on living organisms.
Biological detritus in the water column suspended particulate material
Parameters quantifying and categorising biological detritus (eg exuvia and faecal pellets) in the water column that have been derived from the water column
Parameters describing the nature and intensity of light generated by biological activity in the water column.
Parameters describing the actions or reactions of birds (Class Aves), usually in response to the environment. Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.
Parameters related to the reproduction of birds (Class Aves)
Bird taxonomy-related abundance per unit area of surface

Bird (Class Aves) abundance per unit area (of land or sea) presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy.These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.

Bird (Class Aves) count parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards. Count includes presence/absence indicators.

Concentrations of total, organic and inorganic carbon per unit weight of sediment. Sediment is understood to be the solid phase of the bed, including the recently settled material sometimes known as fluff collected from the bed surface.
Carbon concentrations in suspended particulate material
Concentrations of total, organic and inorganic carbon per unit weight of suspended particulate material collected by water column filtration, centrifugation or sediment trapping.
Carbon monoxide and dioxide concentrations in the atmosphere
CO and CO2 concentration parameters in any phase of the atmosphere (but usuall the gaseous phase). Includes pCO2.
Sediment includes anything collected by a grab or corer, including the fluff layer from the top of the consolidated sediment
Carotenoid pigment concentrations in the water column
Parameters that specify the number of specified members of Order Cetacea present at a particular time and location, including presence/absence indicators.

Parameters describing the actions or reactions of cetaceans (Order Cetacea), usually in response to the environment. Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.

Parameters describing the size, shape or physiological activity including disease and parasite infection status of cetaceans (Order Cetacea). Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.
Parameters describing the causes and rate of mortality in cetaceans (Order Cetacea). Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.
Parameters related to the reproduction of cetaceans (Order Cetacea)
Chlorofluorocarbon concentrations in the water column
Concentrations of chlorofluorocarbons (also known as freons or CFCs) in sny body of water
Includes all variants of chlorophyll. Sediment includes anything collected by a grab or corer, including the fluff layer from the top of the consolidated sediment
Chlorophyll pigment concentrations in the water column
Includes all variants of chlorophyll expressed in terms of per unit volume or unit area of the water column. Does not include data expressed per unit mass of SPM.
Parameters describing the horizontal and vertical extent of cloud cover
Parameters that classify cloud cover into types such as cumulus and cirrus.
All parameters associated with coastal landforms such as beaches and dunes including morphology, evolution and associated transport phenomena
Colloidal metal concentrations in the water column
Concentrations of metal elements in the colloidal phase of the water column. Usually the dissolved concentration difference between conventionally filtered water and ultra-filtered water.
Colloidal organic carbon concentration in the water column
Colloidal organic carbon per unit volume of the water column.
Concentration of adenlylates in the water column
Concentrations of adenylates (ADP, ATP etc) in all phases of the water column
Concentrations of adenylates (ADP, ATP etc) per unit mass or unit volume of sediment (material collected by a corer including fluff)
Concentration of alkanamines (amines) in the water column
Alkanamine concentrations in all phases of the water column
Concentration of alkanes in sediment samples
Alkane concentrations in sediment, which is considered to be anything from the bed sampled by a grab or corer, including 'fluff'
Concentration of alkanes in the atmosphere
Alkane concentrations in all phases of the atmosphere
Concentration of alkanes in the water column
Alkane concentration parameters (including saturation of gaseous species) in all phases of the water column. Does not include parameters expressed per unit weight of SPM.
Concentration of alkenes and alkynes in the atmosphere
Alkene and alkyne concentrations in all phases of the atmosphere
Concentration of alkenes and alkynes in the water column
Alkene and alkyne concentrations in all phases of the water column
Concentration of alkenones and alkenoates in the water column
Concentrations of alkenones and alkenoates in all phases of the water column
Concentration of carbohydrates, phenols, alkanols (alcohols), aldehydes and ketones in water bodies
Concentrations of carbohydrates, phenols, alkanols (alcohols), aldehydes and ketones in all phases of any body of fresh or salt water
Concentration of carbohydrates, phenols, alkanols (alcohols), ethers, aldehydes and ketones in sediment
Concentrations of carbohydrates, phenols, alkanols (alcohols), ethers,aldehydes and ketones in unlithified sediment (material collected by a corer including fluff).
Concentration of dissolved organic matter in the water column
Concentration (not 380nm light absorption) parameters for dissolved organic matter (includes humics, yellow matter, Gelbstoff) in the water column
Concentration of inorganic halogens in sediment pore waters
Concentrations of halogens as elements or their inorganic compounds in all phases of sediment pore water
Concentration of inorganic halogens in the atmosphere
Concentrations of halogens as elements or their inorganic compounds in all phases of the atmosphere.
Concentration of inorganic halogens in water bodies
Concentrations of halogens as elements or their inorganic compounds in all phases of any body of fresh or salt water
Concentration of inorganic sulphur species in sediment
Concentration parameters for inorganic sulphur species in sediment (anything collected by a corer including fluff)
Concentration of inorganic sulphur species in sediment pore water
Concentration parameters (including saturation if gaseous) for inorganic sulphur species in all phases of sediment pore waters
Concentration of inorganic sulphur species in suspended particulate material

Concentration parameters for inorganic sulphur species in suspended particulate material (anything collected by filtration or sediment trapping). Group does not include parameters expressing data per unit volume of the water column
Concentration of inorganic sulphur species in the water column
Concentration parameters (including saturation if gaseous) for inorganic sulphur species in all phases of the water column
Concentrations (ie quantity per unit mass or volume, but not relative abundance profiles) of lipids in any type of biological sample
Concentration of nitrogen species in the atmosphere
Concentrations of both organic (eg amines) and inorganic (eg ammonia and oxides of nitrogen) nitrogen species in all phases of the atmosphere
Concentration of nucleic acids in sediment
Concentrations of nucleic acids (DNA, RNA etc.) per unit mass or unit volume of sediment (material collected by a corer including fluff)
Concentration of nucleic acids in water bodies
Parameters quantifying the amount of cell nucleus material (RNA, DNA, gene copies) in any body of salt or fresh water.
Concentration of organic matter in sediments
Parameters quantifying the proportion of organic material in a soil or sediment sample
Concentration of organic matter in the atmosphere
Parameters quantifying uncategorised organic substance concentrations in atmospheric, generally aerosol, samples such as organic matter and DOC.
Concentration of other hydrocarbons in the atmosphere
'Other' (not alkanes, alkenes, alkynes or PAHs) hydrocarbon concentration parameters (including saturation of gaseous species) in all phases of the atmosphere.
Concentration of other hydrocarbons in the water column

'Other' (not alkanes, alkenes, alkynes or PAHs) hydrocarbon concentration parameters (including saturation of gaseous species) in all phases of the water column. Does not include parameters expressed per unit weight of SPM.
Concentration of other organic contaminants in biota
Concentration parameters for carbon compounds regarded as environmentally harmful in either whole organisms or their constituent parts that are not included in other categories
Concentration of other organic contaminants in sediment samples

Concentration parameters for carbon compounds regarded as environmentally harmful in sediment, which is considered to be anything from the bed sampled by a grab or corer, including 'fluff' that are not included in other specific categories
Concentration of other organic contaminants in suspended particulate material

'Other' organic contaminant (substances regarded as harmful other than PCBs and PAHs) concentrations in suspended particulate material, regarded as anything sampled by a water bottle, SAP, sediment trap etc. This group is for SPM composition measurements (concentration per unit weight) and NOT concentrations per unit volume of the water column in the particulate phase.
Concentration of other organic contaminants in the atmosphere
Parameters quantifying concentrations of organic contaminants (substances regarded as harmful) other than PCBs and PAHs in all phases of the atmosphere
Concentration of other organic contaminants in the water column

Concentration parameters for carbon compounds regarded as environmentally harmful in solution or suspension (i.e.includes measurements in both the dissolved and particulate phases) in any body of salt or fresh water that are not included in other specific categories
Concentration of other substances in biota

'Other' (than metals or organic contaminants) substance concentrations in either whole organisms or their constituent parts. This is a 'bucket' grouping that may be reclassified as the dictionary developes.
Parameters associated with the concentration of algae-generated toxins in either whole organisms or their constituent parts
PCB concentrations in either whole organisms or their constituent parts
Concentration of polychlorobiphenyls (PCBs) in sediment samples
PCB concentrations in sediment, which is considered to be anything from the bed sampled by a grab or corer, including 'fluff'
Concentration of polychlorobiphenyls (PCBs) in suspended particulate material

PCB concentrations in suspended particulate material, regarded as anything sampled by a water bottle, SAP, sediment trap etc. This group is for SPM composition measurements (concentration per unit weight) and NOT concentrations per unit volume of the water column in the particulate phase.
Concentration of polychlorobiphenyls (PCBs) in the atmosphere
Parameters quantifying polychlorobiphenyl (PCB) concentrations in all phases of the atmosphere
Concentration of polychlorobiphenyls (PCBs) in the water column
PCB concentrations in all phases of the water column. This group excludes SPM composition measurements (concentration per unit weight).
Concentration of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in biota
PAH concentrations in either whole organisms or their constituent parts
Concentration of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in sediment samples
PAH concentrations in sediment, which is considered to be anything from the bed sampled by a grab or corer, including 'fluff'
Concentration of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in suspended particulate material

PAH concentrations in suspended particulate material, regarded as anything sampled by a water bottle, SAP, sediment trap etc. This group is for SPM composition measurements (concentration per unit weight) and NOT concentrations per unit volume of the water column in the particulate phase.
Concentration of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the atmosphere
Parameters quantifying polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) concentrations in all phases of the atmosphere
Concentration of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the water column
PAH concentrations in all phases of the water column. This group includes concentrations per unit volume of the water column in the particulate phase, but not concentrations per unit wieght of SPM.
Concentrations of proteins per unit mass or unit volume of sediment (material collected by a corer including fluff)
Concentration of proteins in the water column
Concentrations of proteins in all phases of the water column
Concentration of silicon species in suspended particulate material

Concentration parameters for silicon species (including opal) in SPM (material gathered by filtration or sediment trapping). Only includes parameters expressed per unit mass of SPM and not per unit volume of the water column
Concentration of silicon species in the water column
Concentration parameters for silicon species (including opal) in all phases of the water column
Concentration of suspended particulate material in the water column
Parameters quantifying SPM concentration in the water column by weight, by volume or in terms of turbidity
Concentrations of carboxylic acids and carboxylates in the atmosphere
Parameters quantifying the concentration of acids containing a carboxyl (-C(=O)OH) group, their anions or their salts in any phase of the atmosphere
Contaminant fluxes between the terrestrial and marine environment
Parameters quanitifying the transfer of substances considered harmful from land to sea, including river discharge rates of contaminant species (but not freshwater discharge rates).
Absolute determinations of water column density plus parameters (generally expressed as density anomaly) derived from temperature and salinity
Parameters characterising the environment in which sediments were deposited either by observation or interpretation of sedimentary rocks and unlithified sediments.
Diatom taxonomy-related abundance per unit mass of sediment

Determinations of the abundance of diatom remains in sediment linked to taxonomic identifications that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards
Dissolved amino acid concentrations in the water column
Parameters quantifying the amount of organic compounds containing both a carboxyl group and an amino group dissolved in a body of water.
Dissolved concentration parameters for other gases in sediment pore waters
All concentration parameters for inorganic dissolved gases other than oxygen and the noble gases in sediment pore water samples
Dissolved concentration parameters for other gases in the water column
All concentration parameters for inorganic dissolved gases other than oxygen and the noble gases in the water column
Dissolved inorganic carbon production and respiration in the water column
Parameters related to the rates of TCO2 production and consumption based on light/dark bottle incubations
Dissolved inorganic nitrogen concentration in the water column

Total concentration of all dissolved inorganic nitrogen species in the water column, usually derived by summation of individual nutrient concentrations (NO3+NO2+NH4). Some workers may also include urea.
Dissolved metal concentrations in the water column

Concentrations of metal elements in the dissolved phase of the water column. This may include a contribution from the particulate phase if this has not been totally removed by filtration and the metal in question is reactive (ie detected as if it were dissolved) to the analytical technique used.
Dissolved noble gas concentration parameters in the water column
All concentration parameters including saturations and statistics such as standard deviations
Dissolved organic carbon concentration in the water column
DOC per unit volume of the water column. Note that this includes some parameters that are strictly defined as total carbon, because the water was unfiltered on the assumption that POC was negligible.
Dissolved organic carbon concentrations in sediment pore waters
Concentrations of dissolved organic carbon in sediment pore waters
Dissolved organic carbon uptake and production in the water column
Any parameter relating to the rate of DOC concentration change in the water column
Dissolved oxygen concentration parameters in sediment pore waters
All concentration parameters (including saturation) for dissolved oxygen in sediment pore waters
Dissolved oxygen parameters in the water column
All dissolved oxygen parameters (including saturation and utilisation) for the water column
Dissolved total and organic nitrogen concentrations in the water column
Concentration of total (organic plus inorganic) or organic dissolved nitrogen per unit volume of the water column. Grouped together as organic nitrogen frequently determined as total nitrogen.
Dissolved total or organic phosphorus concentration in the water column
Concentration of total (organic plus inorganic) or organic dissolved phosphorus per unit volume of the water column. Grouped together as organic phosphorus frequently determined as total phosphorus.
Dissolved trace metalloid concentrations in the water column

Concentration parameters for trace metalloid elements in the dissolved phase of the water column. This may include a contribution from the particulate phase if this has not been totally removed by filtration and the metal in question is reactive (ie detected as if it were dissolved) to the analytical technique used. Trace metalloids are considered as B, Ge, As, Sb, Te and Po (but not Si which is classed separately because of its major role in environmental chemistry)
Distribution coefficients in the water column
Distribution coefficients of species between the dissolved and particulate phases of the water column
Electrical conductivity of the water column
Parameters quantifying the flow of electrical current through or the electrical resistance of a body of water at any point between the bed and the atmosphere
Technical parameters that provide information on how well an instrument or data acquisition system is working
Excretion rate parameters in the water column
Includes all parameters relating to all mechanisms of waste release except respiration.
Fauna abundance per unit area of the bed

Any fauna (class Animalia) abundance per unit are of sea, river or lake bed. Broad group overlapping a number of more specific groups that should be used preferentially, but this group is provided as an alternative to one-to-many mappings.
Parameters quantifying the electrical resistance and electrical polarisation of in situ soil and sediment geologic units
Paramaters that quantify the numbers of fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes) at a given location in any body of salt or fresh water.
Parameters quantifying and describing biota take by fishing activities

Parameters describing the actions or reactions of fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chondrichthyes), usually in response to the environment. Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.

Parameters quantifying the mass of fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes)in total or by species per unit area or per unit volume in any body of fresh or salt water expressed in any form (e.g. wet weight, dry weight, carbon, nitrogen, etc.).
Parameters related to the infection of Fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes) by parasites and disease. Includes visual assesements and analytical data.
Paramaters that quantify the size, shape, age and life processes (including mortality) of fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes).
Fish non taxonomy-related abundance per unit volume of the water column
Fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes) abundance per unit volume parameters not included under FATX. Most commonly used for the generic term 'fish' that maps to multiple taxa.
Fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes) size and shape parameters not included under FATM. Most commonly used for the generic term 'fish' that maps to multiple taxa.
Paramaters that quantify the fecundity, reproductive rates or nature of reproduction in fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes).
Fish taxonomy-related abundance per unit area of the bed

Fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chondrichthyes) abundance per unit area of bed (sea, river, lake etc.) parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. Includes animals normally considered as planktonic if they have been returned from sediment samples.
Fish taxonomy-related ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the bed

Fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chondrichthyes) ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of bed (sea, river, lake etc.) parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. Includes animals normally considered as planktonic if they have been returned from sediment samples.

Fish (Osteichthyes, Agnatha and Chrondrichthyes) count parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards. Count includes presence/absence indicators.
Parameters describing the extent, intensity, timing and method of fisheries
Parameters quantifying the capture of non-target species during commercial and non-commercial fishing trips
Gas fluxes between the water column and the atmosphere
Fluxes of any gaseous species from water column to atmosphere
Parameters that describe the the mass per unit volume of any samples of rock or unlithified sediment.
Geological sample magnetic, electrical and acoustic properties
Any parameters quantifying the magnetic (e.g. magnetic susceptibility), electrical (e.g. resistivity) or acoustic (e.g. P-wave propogation speed) of sediment or rock cores and samples
Any parameters quantifying ionising radiation emitted by cores or samples comprising rock, sediment (including surface sediment such as fluff)

Parameters quantifying the properties of rocks and sediments that are relevance to engineering such as physical strength and load-bearing capacity. Includes the disciplines of rock mechanics and soil mechanics.
Parameters quantifying the flux of thermal energy within the solid Earth or between the solid Earth and water bodies or atmosphere.
Parameters relating to the measurement of the Earth's gravity field
Parameters quantifying the amount of groundwater in a given system such as aquifer water level and rate of flow of water through rock formations.
Parameters quantifying the chemistry of terrestrial groundwater bodies such as aquifers and waters percolating through rock formations.
Parameters specifying the physical or chemical environment of a place where an organism is found.
Parameters specifying the vertical and horizontal spatial extent of the ecological character of a place where an organism is found
Parameters describing the location, nature and extent of objects that pose a threat to travel on the water column such as wrecks and obstructions
Heat fluxes between the water column and the atmosphere
Parameters quantifying heat exchange between any body of water and the atmosphere
All parameters relating to horizontal platform travel, including distance run
All forms of horizontal spatial coordinates such as lat/lon and grid references
Horizontal velocity of the water column (currents)
Parameters expressing the velocity (including scalar speeds and directions) of water column horizontal movement, commonly termed Eulerian currents
Measured or stratigraphically estimated age of ice
Parameters specifying the speed and direction of sea or land ice and the stresses associated with this motion.
Parameters that quantify the level of industrial activity or industrial output
Parameters that quantify and specify material output into the environment as a result of industrial activity
Inorganic chemical composition of sediment or rocks

Parameters specifying the proportions of inorganic components (major/minor/trace elements, trace metals etc.) in sediment or rock samples. Major elements includes the H2O+ and H2O- parameters reported by convention in oxide weight per cent geochemical major element analyses.
Inorganic phosphorus species concentrations in the atmosphere
Concentration of inorganic phosphorus species (element or compounds) in any phase of the atmosphere
Inorganic silicon species concentrations in the atmosphere
Concentration of inorganic silicon species (element or compounds) in any phase of the atmosphere
Insect and earthworm taxonomy-related abundance per unit area of the bed

Insect (Class Insecta) and earthworm (Subclass Oligochaeta) abundance per unit area of bed (sea, river, lake etc.) parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. Includes animals normally considered as planktonic if they have been returned from sediment samples. This parameter group has been implemented to separate predominantly freshwater taxa from predominantly marine taxa.
Insect and earthworm taxonomy-related abundance per unit area of the littoral zone
Insect (Class Insecta) and earthworm (Subclass Oligochaeta) abundance per unit area of the littoral zone (between spring tide high and low water) parameters.
Insect and earthworm taxonomy-related ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the bed

Insect (Class Insecta) and earthworm (Subclass Oligochaeta) ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of bed (sea, river, lake etc.) parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. Includes animals normally considered as planktonic if they have been returned from sediment samples. This parameter group has been implemented to separate predominantly freshwater taxa from predominantly marine taxa.
Insect and earthworm taxonomy-related ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the littoral zone
Insect (Class Insecta) and earthworm (Subclass Oligochaeta) ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the littoral zone (between spring tide high and low water) parameters.
Insecta taxonomy-related abundance per unit volume of the water column
Insecta abundance parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Insecta taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column
Insecta carbon biomass parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Lagrangian currents and transport rates in the water column
Parameters expressing the mean nett transport rates within the water column like Lagrangian currents. Note this is an unintentional duplicate of VDFC.
Parameters relating to land surface temperature including fire and other hot spot location
Parameters relating to land (including marshes and the intertidal zone) vegetation
Light absorption in the water column
Parameters relating to the extent of light penetration into the water column
Lipid (fatty acids, sterols or isoprenoid compounds) concentrations in sediment
Lipids are defined as small water-insoluble biomolecules generally containing fatty acids, sterols, or isoprenoid compounds. Sediment is defined as material collected by a corer including fluff).
Lipid (fatty acids, sterols or isoprenoid compounds) concentrations in the water column

Concentrations of lipids in all phases of the water column excluding concentrations of lipid per unit weight of the SPM. Lipids are defined as small water-insoluble biomolecules generally containing fatty acids, sterols, or isoprenoid compounds.
Parameters describing rocks on the basis of physical characteristics such as colour, structure, mineralogy and grain size
Parameters describing the abundance and nature of material classed as refuse introduced to the environment by activities of man.
Macroalgae and seagrass infection and damage
Parameters relating to diseases and parasites of macroalgae (Rhodophycota, Chromphycota, Chlorophycota) and seagrass (Charophyta, Anthophyta) and damage to seagrass beds

Macroalgae (Rhodophycota, Chromphycota, Chlorophycota) and seagrass (Charophyta, Anthophyta) count parameters presented at the level of taxa at any level from sub-species upwards. Count includes presence/absence indicators.
Macroalgae generic abundance in water bodies
Any enumeration (e.g. count, number per litre) of macroalgae (seaweeds) designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. total) in any fresh or salt water body.
Parameterisations of the intensity and inclination of Earth's magnetic field
Parameters relating to human built structures on the coast or offshore and their impact on the environment.

Parameters related to the study of human interaction with the sea through the investigation of associated physical remains, be they vessels, shore side facilities, port-related structures, cargoes, human remains or submerged landscapes
Data parameters that carry information relating to a measured parameter such as measurement temperatures, integration depths, quantities sampled and incubation durations
Metal concentrations in either whole organisms or their constituent parts.
Metal concentrations in sediment pore waters
Concentrations of metal elements in sediment pore waters
Concentration of metal elements in any phase of the atmosphere
Concentration parameters for metallic elements in ice and snow
Metal fluxes between the bed and the water column
Parameters quantifying the exchange of metalsbetween the bed (ie the sediment) and the water column sometimes termed benthic fluxes
Metal ligand parameters in the water column
Parameters concerned with the complexation of metals as ligands in the water column
Metal uptake rates in the water column
Parameters relating to the uptake rates of metals from the dissolved phase into the particulate phase
Microzooplankton generic abundance in water bodies

Any enumeration (e.g. count, number per litre) of microzooplankton (free swimming heterotrophic organisms smaller than 200um) designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. total) in any fresh or salt water body.
Parameters that express the consumption of the phytoplankton population by the microzooplankton. Generally the results of dilution experiments on water samples screened through a 200-micron mesh.
Microzooplankton non taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column
Basically, any microzooplankton carbon biomass measurement that isn't included in parameter group MATC. May include data integrations such as 'total microzooplankton'.
Microzooplankton taxonomic abundance in water bodies

Any enumeration (e.g. count, number per litre) of microzooplankton (free swimming heterotrophic organisms smaller than 200um) designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus or family) in any fresh or salt water body.
Microzooplankton taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column

Microzooplankton carbon biomass parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards., but exclude morphological classifications such as 'heterotrophic flagellate'.
Microzooplankton taxonomy-related biosurface area per unit volume of the water column

Microzooplankton surface area per unit volume of the water column parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Microzooplankton taxonomy-related biovolume per unit volume of the water column
Microzooplankton biovolume parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Chemical analyses of minerals extracted from rocks or sediment or analysed in-situ using techniques like the electron microprobe.
Parameters describing or quantifying the mineralogical composition of rocks and unlithified sediments.
Any parameters relating to molecular biology or genetics

Parameters expressing depth (possibly as pressure) of an instrument on a suspended underwater mooring. These are primarily collected to monitor mooring performance by quantifying knock-down and should not be regarded as instrument z co-ordinates (accurate calibration is rare) or as sea level measurements.
Parameters quantifying the uptake rate of nitrate or gaseous nitrogen by flora and fauna living in any body of salt or fresh water
Nitrate concentration parameters in the water column
Nitrate concentration parameters (including statistical parameters such as standard deviation) in the water column. Includes nitrate+nitrite, which is often loosely referred to as nitrate.
Nitrification rate in the water column
Parameters relating to the rate of nitrification (oxidation of reduced nitrogen such as ammonium) in the water column
Nitrite concentration parameters in the water column
Nitrite concentration parameters (including statistical parameters such as standard deviation) in the water column

Concentrations of total, organic and inorganic nitrogen per unit weight of sediment. Sediment is understood to be the solid phase of the bed, including the recently settled material sometimes known as fluff collected from the bed surface.
Nitrogen concentrations in suspended particulate material

Concentrations of total, organic and inorganic nitrogen per unit weight of suspended particulate material collected by water column filtration, centrifugation or sediment trapping. Note that it is common practice to assume all nitrogen in SPM is organic.
Nutrient concentrations in sediment pore waters
Nutrient (nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, phosphate, silicate and urea) concentrations in sediment pore waters
Nutrient fluxes between the bed and the water column
Parameters quantifying the exchange of nutrients between the bed (ie the sediment) and the water column sometimes termed benthic fluxes
Ocean colour and earth-leaving visible waveband spectral radiation

Parameters associated with the measurement of ocean colour, including visible waveband satellite spectral radiometer measurements, their calibration measurements (spectral water-leaving radiance and reflectance) and chart colour estimates.

Includes all parameters covering the strength of electromagnetic radiation signal return, including absolute measurements of returning signal strength as well as parameters expressed as backscatter (the proportion of transmitted signal returned)
Organic sulphur compound dynamics in the water column
Parameters relating to the rates of creation and consumption of organic sulphur compounds (such as DMS and carbonyl sulphide) in the water column
Organometallic species concentration parameters in biota
All measurements of the quantity or mass of any organometallic compound in any living organisms or their component parts
Organometallic species concentration parameters in sediments
All organometallic compound concentration parameters (including saturations for gaseous species) in all phases of sediments (including pore waters)
Organometallic species concentration parameters in water bodies
All organometallic compound concentration parameters (including saturations for gaseous species) in all phases of any body of fresh or salt water
Organosulphur species concentration parameters in the water column
All organosulphur compound concentration parameters (including saturations for gaseous species) in all phases of the water column
Other fluxes between the bed and the water column
Fluxes of species other than metals and nutrients between the bed (ie the sediment) and the water column sometimes termed benthic fluxes or sediment demand
Other halocarbon concentrations in water bodies

Concentrations of volatile halocarbons (compounds comprising carbon atoms covalently bonded to fluorine, chlorine, bromine or iodine atoms) other than tracers (i.e. freons/chlorofluorocarbons) and contaminants in any body of fresh or salt water.
Other halocarbon dynamics in water bodies

Parameters relating to the rates of creation and consumption of volatile halocarbons (compounds comprising carbon atoms covalently bonded to fluorine, chlorine, bromine or iodine atoms) other than tracers (i.e. freons/chlorofluorocarbons) and contaminants in any body of fresh or salt water.
Bucket group for parameters that cannot be classified elsewhere
Other physical and chemical properties of suspended particulate material
Parameters that do not easily fit into any of the other SPM data categories.
Statistical parameters derived from wave data expressing wave properties other than height, period and direction
Oxygen production and respiration in the water column
Parameters related to the rates of oxygen production and consumption
Ozone and oxygen concentrations in the atmosphere
Ozone and oxygen concentration parameters in any phase of the atmosphere (but usually the gaseous phase)

Parameterisations that describe climatic conditions in the past. Includes climate indices, climate indicators and indirect measurements of climate-related phenomena such as sea level and water table depth.
Partial pressure (pCO2) and fugacity (fCO2) of carbon dioxide in the water column
Particulate amino acid concentrations in the water column
Parameters quantifying the amount of organic compounds containing both a carboxyl group and an amino group in solids suspended in a body of water.
Particulate inorganic carbon concentrations in the water column

Concentrations of inorganic carbon in the particulate phase of the water column as extracted by a fitration technique. This is the particle-bound concentration per unit volume of the water column. Consequently, it is both a function of the SPM concentration in the water column and the concentration of inorganic carbon per unit weight of the SPM.
Particulate metal concentrations in the water column
Concentration parameters for metallic elements in the particulate phase of the water column collected by fitration, centrifugation or sediment trapping
Particulate total and organic carbon concentrations in the water column

Concentrations of total and organic carbon in the particulate phase of the water column as extracted by a filtration technique. This is the particle-bound concentration per unit volume of the water column and is both a function of the SPM concentration in the water column and the concentration of carbon per unit weight of SPM. Total and organic carbon are classed together to circumvent confusion caused by total carbon data sets labelled 'POC' on the assumption that the inorganic carbon fraction is negligible
Particulate total and organic nitrogen concentrations in the water column

Concentrations of total and organic nitrogen in the particulate phase of the water column, which is a function of both the SPM concentration in the water column and the concentration of nitrogen per unit weight of SPM. Note that it is commonly assumed that all particulate nitrogen is organic.
Particulate total and organic phosphorus concentrations in the water column

Concentrations of total and organic phosphorus in the particulate phase of the water column, which is a function of both the SPM concentration in the water column and the concentration of phosphorus per unit weight of SPM.
Particulate trace metalloid concentrations in the water column

Concentration parameters for trace metalloid elements in the particulate phase of the water column collected by fitration, centrifugation or sediment trapping. Trace metalloids are considered as B, Ge, As, Sb, Te and Po (but not Si which is classed separately because of its major role in environmental chemistry)
Parameters quantifying the magnitude of naturally occurring low frequency earth movements such as used for earthquake seismology and natural noise studies.
Concentration parameters for substances synthesised by man to kill other life forms in either whole organisms or their constituent parts.
Concentration parameters for substances synthesised by man to kill other life forms in sediment, which is considered to be anything from the bed sampled by a grab or corer, including 'fluff'.

Concentration parameters for substances synthesised by man to kill other life forms in either solution or suspension (i.e.includes measurements in both the dissolved and particulate phases) in any body of salt or fresh water.
Includes all variants of phaeopigment (chlorophyll degradation products). Sediment is defined as any solids collected by a corer, including fluff..
Phaeopigment concentrations in the water column
Includes all variants of phaeopigment (chlorophyll degradation products) expressed in terms of per unit volume or unit area of the water column. Does not include data expressed per unit mass of SPM.
Concentration parameters for substances synthesised by man to modify bodily function or diagnose, cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent disease in either whole organisms or their constituent parts.

Concentration parameters for substances synthesised by man to modify bodily function or diagnose, cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent disease in sediment, which is considered to be anything from the bed sampled by a grab or corer, including 'fluff'.

Concentration parameters for substances synthesised by man to modify bodily function or diagnose, cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent disease in either solution or suspension (i.e.includes measurements in both the dissolved and particulate phases) in any body of salt or fresh water.
Phosphate concentration parameters in the water column
Phosphate concentration parameters (including statistical parameters such as standard deviation) in the water column
Phosphorus concentrations in suspended particulate material
Concentrations of total, organic and inorganic phosphorus per unit weight of suspended particulate material collected by water column filtration, centrifugation or sediment trapping.
Phycobolin pigment concentrations in the water column
Concentration of phycobolin group pigments such as phycocyanin and phycoerythrin in the water column
Phytoplankton generic abundance in water bodies

Any enumeration (e.g. count, abundance) of free-floating autotrophic biological entities designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. microphytoplankton, ciliate, flagellate) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Phytoplankton generic biomass in water bodies

Any parameterisation of biomass (e.g. wet weight, dry weight, carbon, nitrogen etc.) of free-floating autotrophic biological entities designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. microphytoplankton, ciliate, flagellate) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Phytoplankton taxonomic abundance in water bodies
Any enumeration (e.g. count, abundance) of free-floating autotrophic biological entities designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus, family) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Phytoplankton taxonomic biomass in water bodies

Any parameterisation of biomass (e.g. wet weight, dry weight, carbon, nitrogen etc.) of free-floating autotrophic biological entities identified by their taxonomic names (e.g. family, genus, species) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Phytoplankton taxonomic surface area in water bodies
Any parameterisation of cell surface area of free-floating autotrophic biological entities designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus, family) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Phytoplankton taxonomic volume in water bodies
Any parameterisation of cell volume of free-floating autotrophic biological entities designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus, family) in any body of fresh or salt water.
Plankton abundance per unit volume of the water column
Used for plankton abundance parameters where no differentiation between phytoplankton, microzooplankton or zooplankton is possible
Plankton biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column
Used for plankton carbon biomass parameters where no differentiation between phytoplankton, microzooplankton or zooplankton is possible
Parameters that describe the displacement of platforms or instruments in space relative to various origins
Parameters quantifying the accidental spillage of liquid or dry pollutants from vessels or marine industries. Parameters may include quantities of pollutant, areas affected and event duration.
Parameters relating to all kinds of precipitation (rain, snow, etc.) and water loss from the surface of the Earth
Concentration of any chemical species in water collected from the atmosphere. Includes rain, snow, hail and fog but excludes cloud samples or snow accumulations on the ground.
Primary production in the water column

Parameters associated with the quantification of primary production. This is defined as the fixation of carbon dioxide into either organic or inorganic carbon by living entities and so includes photosynthesis and calcification.
Parameters quantifying the amount of liquids (e.g. ship's ballast) or solids (e.g. dredge spoil) deposited into the water column as a result of man's activities

Includes all parameters covering the strength of emitted microwave radiation return, including absolute measurements of returning signal strength as well as parameters expressed as backscatter (the proportion of transmitted signal returned)
Parameters quantifying the level of radioactive emissions from in-situ geologic units
All parameters associated with radioactivity in either whole organisms or their constituent parts
All parameters associated with radiocativity in the water column, including radiation counts, isotope activities and activity ratios. Activities per unit mass of SPM are included
Parameters as logged by measuring devices, including raw counts/voltages and ADCP relative velocities
Output as logged from any type fluorometer.
Raw concentration parameters from a gas analyser such as a LiCor
Direct output parameters from spectophotometric or chemical in-situ nutrient analysers
Raw parameters (usually membrane current and temperature) from dissolved oxygen sensors
Raw suspended particulate material optical sensor output
Raw parameters (voltages and counts) from in-situ suspended particulate material sensors including transmissometers, nephelometers and in-situ particle sizers
Raw temperature and/or salinity instrument output
Direct output parameters from TS instruments such as thermosalinograph or CTD
Reduction rates of any species in sediment cores
Data record, event, sample or measurement reference numbers
Parameters quantifying the uptake rate of nitrogen from excretion products (ammonium and urea) by flora and fauna living in any body of salt or fresh water
Parameters related to the abundance of reptiles (Class Reptilia)
Parameters relating to diseases and parasites of reptiles (Class Reptilia)
Parameters related to the reproduction of reptiles (Class Reptilia)

Parameters related to the volume of water passing through a point in a river system per unit time, including the rates of freshwater, dissolved material and particulate load discharge from a river into the sea.
Measured or stratigraphically estimated ages of lithified sediments, igneous rock or metamorphic rock.

Parameters decribing aspects of a geologic unit that are the result of bulk chemical, mineralogical or physical changes related to change in the physical or chemical environment. Includes weathering, supergene alteration, hydrothermal alteration and metasomatic effects not considered metamorphic.

Parameters specifying the physical dimensions of the particles comprising lithified sedimentary rocks (including expressions of shape such as aspect ratio) and statistics derived from their variation in a sample (e.g. mean, mode, sorting, skewness).
Parmeters describing the space for fluids or gases within a geologic unit comprising lithified sediments, igneous rock or metamorphic rock.
Parameters that describe the degree to which sedimentary, igneous or metamorphic rocks are able to conduct heat
Parameters quantifying the concentration of sodium chloride in any body of water at any point between the bed and the atmosphere
Measurements and predictions of the displacement of the water column surface from a fixed, stable reference
Measurements of the displacement of the water column surface from a fixed, stable reference expressed as either total pressure or sea pressure
Digital images of the seabed obtained using either still or video cameras
Parameters that specify the number of specified members of Family Phocidae present at a particular time and location, including presence/absence indicators.
Parameters describing the actions or reactions of seals (Family Phocidae), usually in response to the environment. Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.

Parameters describing the size, shape or physiological activity including disease and parasite infection status of seals (Family Phocidae). Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.
Parameters describing the causes and rate of mortality of Seals (Family Phocidae). Includes both parameters mapped to taxa and those mapped to non-taxonomic groupings.
Parameters related to the reproduction of seals (Family Phocidae)
Measurements of optical visibility in the water column
Parameters used to encode information specifying access rights to data, usually in terms of authorised roles
Parameters quantifying the volume, mass or thickness of particulate material that gathers on the seabed per unit time.
Parameters relating to the elucidation of sediment structure by quantifying the proportion of waves from a low energy source reflected by sub-surface layers.
Measured or stratigraphically estimated ages of marine sediments

Parameters specifying the physical dimensions of the particles comprising unlithified sediment (including expressions of shape such as aspect ratio) and statistics derived from their variation in a sample (e.g. mean, mode, sorting, skewness).
Parameters relating to the size, shape and form of microfossils in sediment samples
Parameters quantifying the critera for and extent of sediment resuspension
Parameters that describe the degree to which unlithified sediment is able to conduct heat
Sediment water content, porosity and surface area
Sediment porosity (water content by volume) and water content by weight parameters
Parameters characterising structure in sedimentary rocks and unlithified sediment such as bedding, lamination and bioturbation.
Sedimentation flux of alkenones and alkenoates in the water column
Sedimentation flux of amino acids in the water column
Parameters quantifying the amount of organic compounds containing both a carboxyl group and an amino group sinking vertically as particles through a unit area of a water body in units time.
Sedimentation flux of biological detritus in the water column
Flux of biological detritus (material derived from the water column such as exuvia and faecal pellets) in the water column
Sedimentation flux of carbohydates in the water column
Sedimentation flux of carbon, nitrogen or organic matter in the water column

Fluxes of particulate total, organic and inorganic carbon (including as CaCO3) and nitrogen (often measured as 'total' but assumed to be 'organic'). Organic matter is defined as matter lost on ignition.
Sedimentation flux of identified biota expressed as carbon in the water column
Fluxes of any biota or remains thereof (excluding faecal pellets which are classed as SPM) downwards through the water column
Sedimentation flux of identified biota in the water column
Fluxes expressed as number per unit area per unit time of any biota or remains thereof (excluding faecal pellets which are classed as SPM) downwards through the water column
Sedimentation flux of metals in the water column
Fluxes expressed as amount of metallic element per unit area per unit time
Sedimentation flux of non-metallic inorganic species in the water column
Quantity of any inorganic species such as silicon (opal) and phosphorus passing through unit area of the water column in unit time. Carbon and nitrogen are regarded as organic and explicitly excluded
Sedimentation flux of pigments in the water column
Sedimentation flux of terrestrially derived material in the water column
Fluxes of terrestrial biological or lithological material
Sedimentation flux quantification in the water column
Parameters expressing the total sedimentation flux in terms of particle mass, volume or counts
Parameters relating to the elucidation of geological structure by quantifying the proportion of waves from a high energy source reflected by sub-surface layers.
Parameters relating to the elucidation of geological structure by quantifying the refration of waves from a high energy source by sub-surface layers.
Shellfish abundance and biomass in water bodies

Paramaters that quantify the numbers or amount of living material of shellfish (molluscs - including cephalopods - and crustaceans of interest to fisheries research and commercial fisheries) in any body of fresh or salt water.

Paramaters that quantify the size, shape, age and life processes (including mortality) of shellfish (molluscs - including cephalopods - and crustaceans of interest to fisheries research and commercial fisheries).

Paramaters that quantify the fecundity, reproductive rates or nature of reproduction in shellfish (molluscs - including cephalopods - and crustaceans of interest to fisheries research and commercial fisheries).
A technique for mapping the morphology of the seafloor using a sonar swath projected sideways from a towed underwater vehicle.
Silicate concentration parameters in the water column
Silicate concentration parameters (including statistical parameters such as standard deviation) in the water column
Skin temperature of the water column
Temperature of the water column surface as measured by a radiometer. It does NOT include temperature measurements in the upper few metres of the water column such as thermosalinograph data
Parameters related to the chemical composition of any kind of water sample that was frozen solid at the time of sampling or measurement
Snow and ice mass, thickness and extent
Measurements of quantity (mass), thickness and spatial extent of snow and ice
Snow and ice physical properties and characteristics

Parameters related to physical properties (e.g. colour, density, in-situ temperature) or characteristics (e.g. sea ice type) of any kind of water sample that was in its solid state at the time of sampling or measurement
Parameters quantifying the irradiance of the sun impinging on the Earth's surface in the visible and infra-red waveband, generally accepted as wavelengths between 300 and 3000 nm
Sound velocity and travel time in the water column
Parameters for directional and non-directional spectral wave data, excluding wave directions derived from spectral data.
Measured or stratigraphically estimated ages of secondary mineral deposits in caves. This includes stalactites, stalagmites, flowstone, and crystal growths.
Stable isotope enrichment parameters from measurements on living (at the time of sampling) organisms or parts thereof
Stable isotope enrichment parameters in sediment, including biota-associated parameters such as isotope enrichment in foraminifera tests
Stable isotope enrichment in sediment pore waters
Parameters quantifying the relative proportions of stable isotopes in either the solute or solvent phase of sediment pore waters
Stable isotope enrichment parameters in secondary mineral deposits in caves. This includes stalactites, stalagmites, flowstone, and crystal growths.
Stable isotope enrichment in the atmosphere
Stable isotope enrichment parameters in both the gaseous and aerosol phases of the atmosphere
Stable isotope enrichment in the water column
Stable isotope enrichment parameters in both the dissolved and particulate phases of the water column
Structure and stability of the water column
Parameters describing or predicting water column structure plus parameters quantifying the dynamic stability of that structure
Sulphur species concentrations in the atmosphere
Concentration of sulphur species (element or compounds) in any phase of the atmosphere. Includes sulphur dioxide.
Parameters relating to the abundance, size and morphology of particle aggregates in the SPM
Suspended particulate material grain size parameters
Includes all SPM grain size measurements and derived statistics
Suspended particulate material setting velocity parameters
Parameters that describe the distribution of the degree of hotness within a body of rock or unlithified sediment.
Temperature parameters in any body of water at any point between the bed and the atmosphere excluding the top few microns sampled by radiometers known as the skin
Temperature variation in the water column
Parameters expressing the variation of temperature in the water column either as a function of space or of time
Terrestrial detritus in the water column suspended particulate material
Parameters quantifying and categorising terrestrially-derived detritus (eg dust and pollen) in the water column
Parameters relating to the mapping of terrestrial features, including coastlines
Parameters relating to the water held by land masses such as soil and vegetation moisture content
Parameters relating to structure beneath sea-bed determined by the reflection of seismic energy along multiple parallel tracks.
Total dissolved inorganic carbon (TCO2) concentration in the water column
Total dissolved inorganic carbon (TCO2) in sediment pore waters
Carbonate system parameters (DIC/TCO2, pH, alkalinity, pCO2) in sediment pore waters
Total metal concentrations in water bodies
Concentration parameters for metal elements in the combined dissolved and particulate phases of any body of fresh or salt water.

Concentration parameters for trace metalloid elements in either whole organisms or their constituent parts. Trace metalloids are considered as B, Ge, As, Sb, Te and Po (but not Si which is classed separately because of its major role in environmental chemistry)
Trace metalloid concentrations in sediment pore water

Concentration parameters for trace metalloid elements in water occupying the space between sediment grains. Trace metalloids are considered as B, Ge, As, Sb, Te and Po (but not Si which is classed separately because of its major role in environmental chemistry)
Transmittance and attenuance of the water column
Parameters relating to the rate of electromagnetic radiation intensity decrease as it travels through the water column
Parameters quantifying the level of activity moving people or cargo from one place to another.
Parameters describing the transport of material, heat or energy in the water column
Measured parameters expressing turbulence in the water column plus parameters derived from these measurements
Parameters relating to structure beneath sea-bed determined by the reflection of seismic energy along a single track.
Parameters relating to the intensity of ultra-violet radiation in either the atmosphere or the water column

Includes all pigments that cannot be explicitly classified as chlorophylls, phaeopigments or carotenoids (usually groups of pigments). Sediment includes anything collected by a grab or corer, including the fluff layer from the top of the consolidated sediment.
Unclassified pigment concentrations in the water column

Includes all pigments that cannot be explicitly classified as chlorophylls, phaeopigments or carotenoids. Generally, these are parameters where different pigments have been grouped together. Concentrations are expressed in terms of per unit volume or unit area of the water column. Does not include data expressed per unit mass of SPM.
The identity of the parameter is not declared. Covers cases such as internal working parameters and dummy channels.
Uptake of other nutrients in the water column
Uptake of nutrients other than nitrogen species (ie phosphate and silicate) by the water column
Urea concentration parameters in the water column
Urea concentration parameters (including statistical parameters such as standard deviation) in the water column
Parameters measured by variable fluorescence instruments such as pump and probe and fast repetition rate fluorometers
Parameters quantifying the upward and downward motion of objects mounting sensors or collecting samples.
All vertical spatial parameters including depth, height and pressure when used as an independent variable.
Vertical velocity of the water column (currents)
Vertical water movement parameters including non-directional speeds
Any enumeration (e.g. count, number per square metre) of viruses in any body of fresh or salt water.
Visible waveband radiance and irradiance measurements in the atmosphere

Includes visible waveband measurements at discrete wavelengths and PAR integrated values as photon and energy fluxes. Does not include satellite radiometer and associated calibration parameters (e.g. water-leaving radiance and reflectance)
Visible waveband radiance and irradiance measurements in the water column
Includes measurements at discrete wavelengths and PAR integrated values, measurements as photon and energy fluxes.

Parameters describing the amount in a sample of a tracer (rhodamine, SF6, 3He, etc.) that has been purposely released into a water body to track water mass movements or quantify exchanges with the atmosphere.
Digital images of the water column obtained using either still or video cameras
Parameters quantifying fauna and flora that indicate physical or chemical conditions in the water column such as colonisation depths and abundance of indicator species.
Direct measurements (including visual estimates) plus statistically derived parameters
Statistical parameters derived from wave records to express wave height and period.
Measurements of wave height that are not based on the statistical analysis of wave records, such as heave, surface roughness and visual height estimates
All parameters pertaining to wind velocity in either cartesian or polar co-ordinates. Units are a watchpoint as some codes specify knots.
Parameters related to forces due to interactions between atmosphere and the surface of the earth or between atmospheric air masses
Any enumeration (e.g. count, number per square metre) of animals living on or near the seabed designated by terms other than taxonomic names (e.g. total).
Zoobenthos non taxonomy-related wet weight biomass per unit area of the bed
Any zoobenthos wet weight biomass per unit area of the seabed parameters that are not included in parameter group ZWTX.
Parameters indicating the health of zoobenthos taxa, such as fecundity, egg condition, presence of parasites/diseases etc.
Any enumeration (e.g. count, number per square metre) of animals living on or near the seabed designated by taxonomic names (e.g. species, genus).
Zoobenthos taxonomy-related abundance per unit area of the littoral zone
Any zoobenthos abundance per unit area of the littoral zone (between spring tide high and low water) parameters that are not fish or terrestrial animals (insecta/oligochaeta)
Zoobenthos taxonomy-related ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the bed

Zoobenthos (benthic animals other than insects, Oligochaeta (earthworms) and fish) ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of bed (sea, river, lake etc.) parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. Includes animals normally considered as planktonic if they have been returned from sediment samples.
Zoobenthos taxonomy-related ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the littoral zone
Any zoobenthos ash-free dry weight biomass per unit area of the littoral zone (between spring tide high and low water) parameters that are not fish or terrestrial animals (insecta/oligochaeta)

Zoobenthos count parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards. Count includes presence/absence indicators.
Zoobenthos taxonomy-related wet weight biomass per unit area of the bed

Zoobenthos wet weight biomass per unit area parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. Includes animals considered as planktonic if they have been returned from sediment samples.
Zooplankton and zoobenthos development stage parameters

Development stage parameters (such as proportion but excluding abundance or biomass) of zooplankton and zoobenthos. Benthic and planktonic animals have not been seggregated because there is a degree of overlap (eg shrimps).

Morphological parameters of zooplankton and zoobenthos (essentially any animal except for insects, earthworms or fish), such as size, shape and weight. Benthic and planktonic animals have not been seggregated because there is a degree of overlap (eg shrimps).
Zooplankton ash-free dry weight biomass per unit volume of the water column
Zooplankton (mesozooplankton and larger, exclusing fish, mammals, reptiles and insects) biomass determined by gravimetric measurement of loss on ignition
Zooplankton carbon biomass per unit area of the water column
Integrated zooplankton (mesozooplankton and larger, exclusing fish, mammals, reptiles and insects) carbon biomass parameters
Chemical composition of zooplankton expressed in terms of mass (or molar quantity) per specimen or per unit tissue mass
Zooplankton defecation rates in the water column
Faecal pellet production and gut evacuation rates
Zooplankton dry weight biomass per unit volume of the water column
Zooplankton (mesozooplankton and larger, exclusing fish, mammals, reptiles and insects) biomass determined by drying to constant weight.

Parameters quantifying the ingestion of food by zooplankton (mesozooplankton and larger but excluding fish) in terms of identified biota or chemical species and the effects of nutrition on life processes such as physiology and reproduction.
Parameters pertaining to zooplankton growth rates including biochemical proxies such as AARS activity
Parameters identifying or quantifying zooplankton gut pigments
Zooplankton non taxonomy-related abundance per unit volume of the water column

Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) abundance per unit volume parameters not included in group ZATX. Usually used for generic names such as 'mesozooplankton'.
Zooplankton non taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column

Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) carbon biomass per unit volume parameters not included in group ZCTC. Usually used for generic names such as 'mesozooplankton'.
Zooplankton non taxonomy-related biomass expressed as nitrogen per unit volume of the water column

Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) nitrogen biomass per unit volume parameters not included in group ZCTC. Usually used for generic names such as 'mesozooplankton'.
Zooplankton non taxonomy-related biomass expressed as protein per unit volume of the water column
Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) protein biomass per unit volume for entities that have not been identified by taxonomic name
All parameters related to zooplankton reproduction rates
Zooplankton taxonomy-related abundance per unit volume of the water column

Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) abundance parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Zooplankton taxonomy-related biomass expressed as carbon per unit volume of the water column

Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) carbon biomass parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Zooplankton taxonomy-related biomass expressed as nitrogen per unit volume of the water column

Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) nitrogen biomass parameters presented at the level of taxa that may be mapped to entities in the ITIS taxonomy. These may be at any taxonomic level from sub-species upwards.
Zooplankton taxonomy-related biomass expressed as protein per unit volume of the water column
Zooplankton (mesozooplankton plus larger pelagic animals excluding fish, reptiles and mammals) protein biomass per unit volume for entities that have been identified by taxonomic name
Zooplankton (mesozooplankton and larger, exclusing fish, mammals, reptiles and insects) biomass determined by weighing unprocessed catch samples.
